name: CoinSnap
tagline: Point your phone at a coin, get an identification, rough value, and a place to keep your collection.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The identification half of this is a vision model with a good prompt, and any competent agent can wire that up in an afternoon: camera input, model call, a local database of your coins with photos and notes. The valuation half is where it gets thin, because a market estimate is only as good as the price data behind it, and realized auction prices, grading tiers, and mintage tables are not things a model reliably knows from memory. You will get confident-sounding numbers that are sometimes wildly off, which is arguably also true of the paid apps, but at least they can point at a data source. Build it if you want a searchable personal catalog with an AI first guess. Do not build it if you plan to sell or insure anything based on the output.
coreLoopDIY: Snap or upload a coin photo, send it to a vision model for country, denomination, year, mint mark, and a cautious value range, then save the result with the image into a local collection you can browse and search.
requirements: An OpenAI or Gemini API key with vision access, in .env
A phone on the same network, or just a laptop webcam, for capture
A few cents per scan in model costs
whatYouLose: Any actual price data: realized auction results, grading premiums, and mintage tables are not in the box
Grading guidance that means anything, since condition drives most of a coin's value
A polished native camera flow with autofocus, macro hints, and offline capture
Accumulated correction loops from thousands of users flagging bad identifications
Anything resembling a defensible answer if you are insuring or selling the collection
moatNotes: The identification is a commodity model call. The part you cannot clone is a maintained price and mintage dataset plus the tuning that stops the model from hallucinating a rare variety on a worn 1974 quarter.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the annoying parts are the parts nobody wants to build: a camera flow that works one-handed while holding a coin under a lamp, a value estimate tied to something more real than model recall, and a catalog that syncs to your phone so the collection is with you at a coin show. A local build handles the fun 70 percent and then asks you to care about the other 30 percent forever. For hobbyists who scan a dozen coins a year, a few dollars a month is cheaper than maintaining your own pipeline.
notes: The identifier is a one-sitting build; treat every dollar figure it prints as fiction until you check a real price guide.
prompt:
Build a local web app called "coinshelf" for cataloging a personal coin collection with AI-assisted identification.

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js App Router with TypeScript, Tailwind for styling, SQLite via better-sqlite3 for storage, and the OpenAI API for vision. No auth, no accounts, no cloud storage, no telemetry, no analytics. Single user, runs on localhost.

Core flow:
1. A capture page with a file input that uses capture="environment" so a phone opens the camera directly, plus plain drag-and-drop upload for desktop.
2. On submit, save the image to ./data/images with a generated filename, then send it to a vision model call.
3. The model prompt must ask for strict JSON: country, denomination, year_estimate, mint_mark, composition_guess, diameter_mm_guess, notable_variety, condition_notes, value_range_low, value_range_high, currency, confidence (0 to 1), and reasoning (two sentences max). Instruct the model to return nulls rather than guesses when the image is unclear, and to state in reasoning when the value range is a rough recollection rather than a lookup.
4. Store the parsed JSON plus the raw model response in SQLite alongside the image path and a created_at timestamp.

Collection view:
- Grid of saved coins with thumbnail, country, year, denomination, and confidence badge.
- Text search across all stored fields, plus filters for country and decade.
- Detail page where every AI field is editable and an "owner verified" flag can be set. Edits win over model output everywhere in the UI.
- Export the whole collection to CSV and to a JSON file with image paths.

Hard requirements:
- OPENAI_API_KEY lives in .env.local, never in code, and the app shows a clear setup error if missing.
- Every displayed value range carries a visible "estimate, not an appraisal" label. No exceptions, no dismissing it.
- Images stay on disk locally; nothing is uploaded anywhere except the single model call.
- Include a seed script that inserts three fake coins so the UI can be reviewed without burning API credits.

Out of scope, do not build: user accounts, multi-device sync, a native app, live market price scraping, grading submission workflows, marketplace or selling features.

Deliver a README with setup steps, the exact commands to run, and a short honest paragraph on why the value estimates should not be trusted.
